analyst_note: Hormuz Day 88; Naval Blockade Day 45; Project Freedom Pause Day 21; WPA Day 27 Past Statutory Deadline / 90-Day Hard Deadline May 29 (3 Days); Warsh Day 12. Tuesday May 26, 2026 — Congress returns from Memorial Day recess; first of three calendar days before the WPA 90-day hard deadline. This brief reflects the pre-dawn through early-morning picture as of 07:00 Pacific. The dominant development of the overnight cycle: US Central Command conducted self-defense strikes in southern Iran in the early hours of Tuesday morning Iran time — targeting two IRGC boats actively laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz and a surface-to-air missile site in Bandar Abbas that was actively targeting US aircraft. Explosions were confirmed in Bandar Abbas. IRGC responded by shooting down one MQ-9 Reaper and firing on a second MQ-9 and an F-35; the IRGC formally declared its 'legitimate' right to 'reciprocal response' and characterized the US strikes as a ceasefire violation. CENTCOM spokesman Timothy Hawkins stated: 'U.S. forces conducted self-defense strikes in southern Iran today to protect our troops from threats posed by Iranian forces... U.S. Central Command continues to defend our forces while using restraint during the ongoing ceasefire.' Two additional US official sources confirmed the strikes do not indicate the ceasefire is over. The diplomatic track remains nominally operational: the 60-day-ceasefire-extension / Hormuz-reopening / nuclear-negotiation deal framework reported by Axios and CNN on May 24-25 has not been publicly walked back by either side. But the overnight military exchange — mines in the Strait, a US aircraft shot down, a SAM site engaged, Bandar Abbas explosions — is the most kinetically significant ceasefire incident since Project Freedom was paused on May 6. The deal is not dead; the ceasefire is fraying. The separate sticking point from May 25 — Khamenei's formal rejection of the US enrichment demand as 'excessive and outrageous,' and the resulting moratorium gap (Iran: 5 years, US: 20 years, operational floor: 12+) — has not publicly advanced overnight. No Khamenei deal endorsement has been issued. Congress returns this morning to Washington with exactly three legislative days before the WPA 90-day hard deadline on May 29. Kevin Warsh is scheduled to take his operational oath at the Federal Reserve building today — Day 12 of his chairmanship and still without a public economic policy statement. The Columbia River Gorge saw the first post-Memorial Day wildfire activity: fires reported at Sherman County near Biggs Junction (OR) and brush fires near Dallesport and Columbia Hills State Park (WA). vibe.rationale: Vibe 3 — revised down from the May 25 evening's 4 (firmer). The overnight CENTCOM self-defense strikes (two IRGC mine-laying boats + SAM site in Bandar Abbas) and the IRGC shootdown of a US MQ-9 Reaper constitute the most kinetically significant ceasefire incident since Project Freedom was paused on May 6. The IRGC has formally declared a 'legitimate right to reciprocal response' — this is an unresolved threat with no US confirmation that it has been stood down. The case for staying at 4: CENTCOM explicitly characterized the strikes as self-defense and stated 'ceasefire is not over'; two additional US official sources corroborated; the diplomatic framework (60-day extension + Hormuz reopening + nuclear window) has not been publicly walked back by either party; Iran's 'doesn't want the bomb' framing is consistent with deal nuclear commitments; no CENTCOM carrier repositioning signal has emerged; the mine-laying and SAM activity by the IRGC represents a provocation pattern rather than a declared war resumption. The case against dropping to 2: no announced US operational resumption; no CENTCOM strike escalation beyond the two defensive incidents; no Hegseth or Trump escalation authorization; oil market open TBD but overnight moves are not a price collapse signal. The case for vibe 3 as the correct morning read: the IRGC MQ-9 shootdown is categorically different from prior overnight skirmishes — it is direct engagement of a US platform within the pause; the IRGC formal retaliation-right declaration is unresolved; Khamenei has not confirmed the deal template; WPA 3 days away; the morning opens with more unresolved military and diplomatic uncertainty than any morning since May 19 (strike called off). Vibe recovers to 4 on IRGC retaliation threat formally walked back or CENTCOM-Iran mutual de-escalation signal. Upgrades to 5 on Khamenei public deal endorsement or Iranian FM formal text confirmation of nuclear commitments. Drops to 2 on CENTCOM carrier repositioning or IRGC announced retaliatory strike execution.

items.headline: Overnight: CENTCOM Self-Defense Strikes Hit IRGC Mine-Laying Boats + Bandar Abbas SAM Site; IRGC Shoots Down MQ-9, Warns of Retaliation; Ceasefire 'Fraying but Not Over'; Deal Framework Nominally Intact; WPA 3 Days
items.summary: The overnight cycle produced the most kinetically significant ceasefire incident since the May 6 Project Freedom pause. In the early hours of Tuesday morning Iran time, US Central Command conducted 'self-defense strikes' targeting two IRGC boats in the Strait of Hormuz that were actively laying mines and a surface-to-air missile site in Bandar Abbas that was actively targeting US aircraft. Explosions were confirmed in Bandar Abbas — the primary Iranian port on the Hormuz strait. CENTCOM spokesman Timothy Hawkins issued the official characterization: 'U.S. forces conducted self-defense strikes in southern Iran today to protect our troops from threats posed by Iranian forces... Targets included missile launch sites and Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines. U.S. Central Command continues to defend our forces while using restraint during the ongoing ceasefire.' Two additional US official sources confirmed the strikes do not indicate the ceasefire is over. The IRGC responded operationally and rhetorically. Operationally: Iran's air defense shot down one MQ-9 Reaper drone and fired on a second MQ-9 and an F-35 Lightning II. Rhetorically: the IRGC issued a formal statement via Fars News Agency declaring its 'legitimate' right to 'reciprocal response' and characterizing the US strikes as a ceasefire violation. As of 07:00 Pacific, the IRGC retaliation threat has not been walked back, no further US strikes have been confirmed, and no CENTCOM carrier repositioning signal has emerged. The analytical read on the incident: the IRGC's mine-laying activity in the Strait is consistent with a pattern of testing ceasefire terms while maintaining deniability — mines are slow-action anti-access weapons that create risk without constituting an immediate attack. The SAM site activation targeting US aircraft is a more direct provocation. CENTCOM's response was calibrated — destroying the active threat vectors while explicitly characterizing the action as defensive and the ceasefire as continuing. The IRGC's MQ-9 shootdown is the most significant Iranian anti-US platform action since the war paused; it will generate pressure from US military leaders for a more forceful response unless IRGC stand-down signals emerge quickly. The diplomatic implication: the overnight exchange does not collapse the deal framework, but it demonstrates that the IRGC — which the May 25 analysis identified as a potential deal-track spoiler if hardliners interpreted Khamenei's 'excessive' rejection as license for continued resistance — is actively testing ceasefire limits during the most sensitive diplomatic window of the conflict cycle. On the broader deal picture: the 60-day ceasefire extension + Hormuz gradual reopening + Iran oil sanctions waivers + 60-day nuclear negotiation window framework reported by Axios and CNN on May 24-25 has not been publicly walked back by either party's diplomatic leadership. Iran's official position — 'doesn't want the bomb' — is consistent with the deal's never-pursue-nuclear-weapons commitment. Abbas Araghchi's team has not issued a formal text rejection. The moratorium gap (Iran: 5 years, US: 20 years, operational floor per sources: 12+) and Khamenei's May 25 'excessive and outrageous' rejection of US enrichment demands remain the active nuclear sticking points. No Khamenei public endorsement of the deal template has emerged overnight. The WPA 90-day hard deadline is 3 days away. Congress returns today with three legislative days before May 29. No emergency pre-deadline session has been announced; House Republican leadership has explicitly scheduled the next war powers vote for early June.

items.headline: Quad Foreign Ministers New Delhi Today — Rubio, Jaishankar, Penny Wong, Toshimitsu Motegi; Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire Day 10 Holding; CISA Day 23 Post-Memorial Day Gap Closed Clean
items.summary: Three secondary geopolitical threads opening the day. First: the Quad foreign ministers formal ministerial session convenes in New Delhi today — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, India External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, Australia FM Penny Wong, and Japan FM Toshimitsu Motegi. This is India's first Quad foreign ministers host since 2023. The agenda: critical minerals coordination, maritime security, HADR frameworks, pharmaceutical supply chain resilience, and preliminary planning for the long-delayed Quad Leaders' Summit. The timing is significant: Rubio issued his 'another way' military warning from New Delhi on May 25 and simultaneously called the deal framework 'a pretty solid thing on the table.' Today's Quad ministerial operationalizes that dual-track posture — maintaining Indo-Pacific alliance architecture as a parallel priority to Iran bilateral diplomacy. Overnight, the IRGC mine-laying and SAM site activity in Hormuz will now provide context for the Quad discussion of maritime security and free navigation in contested waterways. Watch for any Quad joint statement on Hormuz navigation principles and whether the communiqué addresses the overnight CENTCOM strikes. Second: the Israel-Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension advances to Day 10 without confirmed violations. The overnight CENTCOM-IRGC exchange modestly raises the second-front probability: if IRGC hardliners are in active resistance mode (as the mine-laying suggests), Hezbollah-linked escalation in Lebanon is a non-trivial parallel track. The ceasefire holds as of this filing; the holding condition is tied to overall Iran deal viability. Next ceasefire talks: June 2-3. Third: CISA Day 23. The Memorial Day federal monitoring gap — identified in the May 25 brief as the highest-priority cyber window of the weekend — closed without confirmed OT/ICS incident. Federal SOC, watch-floor, and CISA/FBI response teams returned to standard staffing this morning as Congress resumed. The overnight CENTCOM strikes introduce a new IRGC cyber calculus modifier: IRGC hardliners who executed the mine-laying and SAM activation overnight may be in operational mode; a cyber escalation as a parallel retaliation channel (consistent with the IRGC's historical 'many tools' posture) remains a live risk on the first post-holiday operational day.

items.headline: Warsh Day 12: Operational Fed Oath Scheduled This Morning; Markets Open to Overnight CENTCOM Strike Premium vs. Deal Optimism; 30-Year at 2007 High; June FOMC 22 Days; No Policy Statement Issued
items.summary: Kevin Warsh enters Day 12 as Federal Reserve Chair — still without a single public economic policy statement — with an operational oath scheduled at the Federal Reserve building today, a second ceremony distinct from the May 22 White House swearing-in with Justice Clarence Thomas. The Fed building oath formally marks Warsh's institutional assumption of the Chair role under Fed procedural protocol. The morning market context he inherits: overnight CENTCOM self-defense strikes in southern Iran and the IRGC MQ-9 shootdown create an escalation premium at the open, pushing oil prices above the May 25 Memorial Day lows. Brent crude is expected to open in the $103-107 range — the escalation premium from IRGC mine-laying activity in the Strait partially offsetting the deal-track softness that drove Brent toward the $100 psychological floor on May 25. WTI is expected to recover from the $91 May 25 low toward the $93-96 range, contingent on whether markets read the overnight exchange as a ceasefire-testing provocation (contained) or a resumption signal (not contained, per CENTCOM). The critical economic read: Warsh's 12-day communication vacuum now encompasses the most volatile oil price cycle of any recent Fed chair transition. April CPI stands at 3.8% YoY — the highest since May 2023 — with energy costs up 17.9% annually (gasoline +28.4%). The 10-year Treasury yield holds near 4.57%; the 30-year at the 5.07-5.18% range, the latter a 2007 high. Bloomberg's morning read: the bond market is opening the 'Warsh Era' with investors pricing in a 2026 rate increase — Fed funds futures placing roughly 40% probability on a December hike and near-zero probability on a cut at any remaining 2026 FOMC meeting. This is the inverse of the rate-cut mandate that drove the political process around Warsh's appointment. The structural explanation per Bloomberg: 'the biggest inflation surge since 2023' (the Iran war) has flipped the bond market's rate expectation from Powell-era pause to Warsh-era potential hike. Warsh's operational oath today does not produce an economic policy statement by itself — but markets and journalists will be watching for any remarks at the ceremony. June FOMC is 22 days out. The Fed funds rate holds at 3.50-3.75% for a third consecutive meeting — the most recent decision carried four dissenting votes, the highest FOMC internal disagreement in decades. A deal signed this week would initiate the disinflationary pathway; pump-price relief to consumers is minimum 4-6 weeks from any confirmed deal. The structural energy floor — AI/data-center electrification demand, $20B+ grid investment cycle, utility capex $1.1-1.4T through 2030 — persists independent of Hormuz resolution.

items.summary: The CISA post-summit clean streak extends to Day 23 with the Memorial Day federal monitoring gap closing without confirmed OT/ICS incident. Federal SOC, watch-floor, and CISA/FBI response teams are back to standard staffing as of this morning. However, the IRGC's overnight operational activity — mine-laying in the Hormuz strait, SAM site activation targeting US aircraft, and the MQ-9 shootdown — materially modifies the morning cyber threat calculus. The IRGC's overnight mode is active resistance rather than passive waiting; the MQ-9 shootdown is the most direct IRGC-attributed destruction of a US platform during the pause phase. Historically, IRGC kinetic operations and IRGC cyber operations have been run in parallel as a 'many tools' escalation approach — the CISA April 7 advisory explicitly warned that Iranian-affiliated actors 'exploit PLCs in US critical infrastructure' including water, wastewater, energy, government facilities, and transportation. The IRGC Cyber Electronic Command (CyberAv3ngers / Shahid Kaveh Group, Handala) retains full demonstrated PLC exploitation capability. The risk calculus this morning: IRGC in an active kinetic resistance mode during a ceasefire has historically been the precondition for a parallel cyber escalation; the first post-Memorial Day operational day, with normal staffing returned, is the highest-threat window since the gap opened. The May 12 advisory also covers the Defense Industrial Base and Israeli-linked corporate nodes — both of which remain relevant given the Quad ministerial and the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire's parallel dependency on the Iran deal track. Standard elevated monitoring is operative; the IRGC overnight activity vector does not trigger maximum priority but warrants heightened FINRA, NERC, and FBI/IC3 feed monitoring throughout the morning.

items.summary: Oregon fire season advances to Day 19 as the first confirmed post-Memorial Day wildfire activity emerges in the Columbia River Gorge. A fire broke out Saturday afternoon in Sherman County near milepost 105 east of Biggs Junction, creating visibility problems as smoke drifted across the Interstate 84 corridor. Brush fires were also reported near Dallesport and Columbia Hills State Park on the Washington side of the Gorge, prompting evacuation notices for portions of Horsethief Park. These are the first named fire activity reports of the 2026 season in the Gorge — an area with historical severity (the 2017 Eagle Creek fire) and high human-caused ignition risk along the I-84 corridor. The post-Memorial Day assessment window opens this morning: BLM, ODF, and NWS morning reports will reveal the full scope of holiday weekend fire activity. Level 1 fire restrictions have been fully operative across Central Oregon (Deschutes, Ochoco, Crooked River national forests and grasslands) since May 18 — Day 8. BLM full Oregon-Washington restrictions are at Day 13, effective May 14. The baseline seasonal context is unchanged: 82% statewide Oregon drought, Southern Cascades in the 'extreme' category, ECMWF -3.98-inch Pacific Coast precipitation anomaly through July, snowpack approximately one-third of normal. East Cascades above-normal onset (June 1, NIFC) is now 6 days away. Forest Service Region 6 structural capacity remains unaddressed: 1,400+ certified firefighter-eligible positions lost to DOGE-related cuts, $0 forest research in the Trump budget. Congress returned today — Oregon congressional Democrats' May 7 letter is now 19 days unanswered, and the first federal legislative response opportunity arrived this morning. Three legislative days remain before June 1. Separately, the Bureau of Reclamation began rationing water to Central Washington irrigators on May 21 — a direct structural impact on agricultural output in one of the nation's most productive belts, arriving five days before fire season onset and concurrent with the green card reversal labor uncertainty.

items.headline: Congress Returns Day 1: WPA 3 Days to May 29 Hard Deadline — No Emergency Session; Deal Framework Does Not Reset Clock; Gabbard DNI Vacancy at Deal-Critical Moment; Warsh Operational Oath Today
items.summary: Congress returned from Memorial Day recess this morning — the first of three calendar days before the WPA 90-day hard deadline on May 29. As of this filing, no emergency pre-deadline session has been announced, no pre-deadline House war powers vote has been scheduled, and no Senate 8th resolution has been filed. House Republican leadership has explicitly scheduled the next war powers vote for early June — after the deadline. The bipartisan House majority coalition (Rep. Jared Golden confirmed yes, six Republicans) is real but has been dormant since the May 22 cancellation. The three-day pre-deadline window (May 26-28) is the final opportunity for any legislative response before May 29's legal architecture change. The critical analytical clarification: the deal framework — even if signed today — does not reset the WPA clock. Under any reading of the statute, cessation of hostilities requires the Strait of Hormuz to be physically open, the naval blockade to be lifted, and conflict-related military operations to have ended. With Hormuz physically closed (overnight mine-laying), the blockade active, and CENTCOM strikes executed in the last 12 hours, none of the physical preconditions for cessation are met. Even if a formal deal text were signed and announced today, Hormuz transit normalization requires days to weeks. The WPA threshold cannot be crossed before May 29 under any plausible timeline. A second significant structural gap: Tulsi Gabbard resigned as Director of National Intelligence on May 22. The DNI vacancy — with an acting director in place but no confirmed permanent appointment — is heading into the most consequential deal-verification week of the conflict cycle. Last night's IRGC mine-laying and SAM activation are precisely the kind of intelligence-assessment challenge that requires a fully empowered DNI to coordinate cross-agency response. The overnight CENTCOM strikes also generate a congressional War Powers notification requirement; watch for a White House notification to Congress as part of the return-day proceedings. Kevin Warsh takes his operational Fed oath at the Federal Reserve building today — the institutional formality completing his assumption of the Chair role. No economic policy statement is expected from the ceremony; but markets and press will be monitoring for any off-the-cuff remarks.

items.headline: Measles School Window Effectively Closed — National 1,952; OHA 35 Days Stale; 'One Big Beautiful Bill' Senate Floor Week; Green Card Reversal PNW Labor Risk 5 Weeks Out; Portland $172M First Post-Recess Council Session
items.summary: Four secondary domestic threads. First: the organized school-based vaccination window has closed. The national measles count stands at 1,952 confirmed cases as of May 21 (pace ~8.4/day, up 59 from May 14). Oregon Health Authority data is now 35 days stale — last published 20 confirmed Oregon cases on April 22 with no update in over a month. Yesterday (May 25, Memorial Day) was the last day any school-based outreach infrastructure could theoretically have operated, and it was a federal holiday. Washington DOH publishes Monday/Wednesday/Friday; a Monday May 26 update should be expected today, reflecting Kittitas County and broader outbreak activity through the holiday weekend. Community health centers and outpatient clinical settings are now the de facto primary intervention channels. The critical escalation watches: new county outbreak declaration, a second Oregon hospitalization (first was April, patient discharged recovering), or any school end-of-year exposure event. Second: the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' (H.R. 1 / OBBBA) reconciliation package is targeting the Senate floor this week with the President's desk by June 1 (6 days). The Senate Judiciary/Homeland Security committee version adds $72B+ for immigration enforcement and defense: ICE ($38B), CBP ($26B), White House security. The bill's immigration enforcement provisions interact directly with the green card policy reversal now in effect. Third: the Trump administration's May 22 green card reversal — requiring foreign nationals seeking lawful permanent residence to leave the US and apply from their home country — is in effect. USCIS implementation guidance remains pending. The PNW agricultural labor intersection is 5-6 weeks away: late June, when fire season crew needs and harvest season labor demand (Columbia Basin, Willamette Valley, Yakima Valley) converge. Any labor supply shortfall at this intersection simultaneously compresses fire crew recruitment and agricultural production. Fourth: Portland City Council holds its first post-Memorial Day recess session today with a $172 million structural shortfall unaddressed. No emergency budget session has been called; council action is required but not yet scheduled.

items.summary: The Pacific Northwest fire season surfaced its first post-Memorial Day fire activity in the Columbia River Gorge. A fire broke out Saturday afternoon in Sherman County near milepost 105 east of Biggs Junction, creating smoke-driven visibility problems across the Interstate 84 corridor — one of the primary freight and travel arteries connecting the Portland metro to the inland Northwest. Brush fires were also reported near Dallesport and Columbia Hills State Park on the Washington side of the Gorge, prompting evacuation notices for portions of Horsethief Park. The Gorge is a historically critical ignition zone: it is the most-traveled east-west corridor in the Pacific Northwest, with high human-caused ignition risk from vehicle sparks, campfires, and roadside activity. The 2017 Eagle Creek fire — human-caused, burning 50,000+ acres — is the reference event. BLM full Oregon-Washington restrictions (Day 13) and Level 1 Central Oregon restrictions (Day 8) remain operative, but the Gorge fires indicate ignition activity is already present at the leading edge of the above-normal window. The east Cascades above-normal onset threshold is 6 days away (June 1, NIFC predictive outlook). The post-Memorial Day assessment is opening: morning BLM, ODF, and NWS reports will reveal whether additional fires from the holiday weekend are active. Congress returned today with the first legislative response opportunity for the 19-day-unanswered Oregon Democrats' delegation letter (May 7) on Forest Service capacity gaps. Three legislative days remain before June 1. The Bureau of Reclamation's water rationing to Central Washington irrigators — now in Day 5 since May 21 — adds a structural agricultural stress compounding the fire season: reduced water availability in the Columbia Basin reduces crop resilience to heat and drought, directly affecting the agricultural output of Washington's most productive farming region. National Weather Service forecasters have named the Pacific Northwest as the nation's hottest summer hotspot, with better than 60% probability of above-normal temperatures across the region for June, July, and August — the highest such forecast nationally. Oregon, Idaho, and eastern Washington are already in drought. Oregon's 2025-2026 winter was tied with 1934 as the warmest on record; snowpack is approximately one-third of normal.

items.headline: OR Gas $5.35 / WA $5.78 Records — Overnight Escalation Premium Firms Deal-Conditional Pump Relief Timeline; OHA Measles 35 Days Stale; Green Card Labor Intersection 5 Weeks; Portland $172M First Post-Recess Council
items.summary: Four PNW threads. First: Oregon gasoline holds at $5.35 per gallon (record 2026 high, 4th-highest nationally) and Washington at approximately $5.78. The overnight CENTCOM strikes and IRGC MQ-9 shootdown introduce an escalation premium to oil prices at the morning open, partially reversing the Memorial Day deal-optimism softness that drove WTI toward $91. Brent is expected at $103-107 at open, with the escalation premium pushing back against deal-conditional disinflation. The deal framework's pump-relief pathway — minimum 4-6 weeks from any signed deal — now begins against a higher oil baseline than Monday's close. Any IRGC retaliation execution would extend the pump-relief timeline indefinitely; any IRGC stand-down + deal signing this week restores late-June pump-relief scenario. Second: Oregon Health Authority measles data stands at 35 days stale — last published 20 confirmed Oregon cases on April 22. National count: 1,952 as of May 21, pace ~8.4/day. Washington DOH publishes Monday/Wednesday/Friday; a Monday May 26 update is expected today — any WA update will be the first new measles intelligence available since Friday. The organized school vaccination window has closed; community and outpatient settings are the de facto primary channels. The first-response threshold that would trigger emergency public health action: new county outbreak declaration, second Oregon hospitalization, or a school end-of-year exposure event. Third: the Trump administration green card reversal (May 22) is in effect with USCIS implementation guidance still pending. The critical PNW labor intersection is 5 weeks away — late June, when fire season crew needs (accelerating in the Gorge and east Cascades) and harvest labor demand (Columbia Basin, Willamette Valley, Yakima Valley) converge. With Columbia Gorge fires active this morning and east Cascades onset 6 days away, the fire-crew labor demand is not a theoretical future risk — it is arriving now. Any USCIS guidance restricting seasonal agricultural worker availability compounds directly against firefighting crew recruitment in the same regional labor pool. Fourth: Portland's $172 million structural budget shortfall enters the first post-recess City Council session today. No emergency budget action has been announced. The compound PNW stress vector — first post-holiday Gorge fires + summer hotspot forecast + Bureau of Reclamation irrigation rationing + fire season onset 6 days out + gas records + measles window closed + green card labor risk 5 weeks out + municipal fiscal strain — has reached its highest coherence of the conflict cycle.

analyst_summary: Tuesday May 26, 2026 Morning — Hormuz Day 88, Naval Blockade Day 45, Project Freedom Pause Day 21, WPA Day 27 Past Statutory Deadline / 3 Days to May 29 Hard Deadline, Warsh Day 12. Vibe 3. The morning picture opens harder than the May 25 evening's 4 (firmer) on a single dominant overnight development: CENTCOM self-defense strikes in southern Iran. US Central Command struck two IRGC boats laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz and a SAM missile site in Bandar Abbas that was actively targeting US aircraft. The IRGC shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper and fired on a second MQ-9 and an F-35. Bandar Abbas explosions were confirmed. CENTCOM has explicitly stated the ceasefire is 'not over' and characterized the strikes as defensive; two additional US officials corroborated the containment characterization. But the IRGC has formally declared a 'legitimate right to reciprocal response' — and as of 07:00 Pacific, that threat is unresolved. The analytical read: the IRGC mine-laying activity in Hormuz and SAM site activation are consistent with a hardliner resistance-testing pattern — the same dynamic Khamenei's May 25 'excessive and outrageous' rejection of US enrichment demands may have emboldened. CENTCOM's calibrated self-defense response was tactically correct and diplomatically contained, but the MQ-9 shootdown is categorically different from prior overnight skirmishes. The deal framework (60-day Hormuz reopening + 60-day nuclear negotiation window + sanctions waivers) remains nominally operative — neither Araghchi nor Iran's diplomatic leadership has walked it back. Khamenei has still not publicly endorsed the deal template; the nuclear moratorium gap (Iran: 5 years, US: 20 years, floor: 12+) remains unresolved from May 25. Congress returns this morning to Washington with exactly three legislative days before the WPA 90-day hard deadline on May 29. No emergency pre-deadline session has been announced; the deal framework, even if signed today, does not reset the WPA clock — Hormuz is physically closed and mine-laying is active. Kevin Warsh takes his operational oath at the Federal Reserve building today, Day 12 of his chairmanship and 12 consecutive days without a public economic policy statement. The Fed opens the day without a public position on overnight oil escalation, the IRGC mine-laying, or the deal framework's status. The 10-year holds near 4.57%, the 30-year at a 2007 high, and Bloomberg is characterizing the Warsh era's opening bond market move as pricing a 2026 rate increase rather than the rate cuts that drove his political appointment. In the Pacific Northwest: the Columbia River Gorge produced the first confirmed post-Memorial Day wildfire activity — a fire in Sherman County near Biggs Junction along the I-84 corridor and brush fires near Dallesport and Columbia Hills State Park, Washington, with Horsethief Park evacuation notices. The post-holiday assessment window is opening. Fire season Day 19 with east Cascades above-normal onset 6 days away and the Forest Service Region 6 capacity gap (1,400+ positions) still unaddressed — the first federal response opportunity arrived this morning with Congress's return. Bureau of Reclamation water rationing to Central Washington irrigators continues (Day 5). NWS names PNW as the nation's summer hotspot at 60%+ above-normal probability for June-August. Oregon gas at $5.35 and Washington at $5.78 — overnight escalation premium is pushing the pump-relief timeline out against a firmer oil floor. Vibe 3: deal fraying at the edges but intact at the core; overnight military exchange elevated to MQ-9-shootdown significance; IRGC retaliation threat unresolved; Khamenei confirmation outstanding; WPA deadline imminent.
